question: Which inactive ingredients do the medicine labels on MoleculeFinder list, and which labels list each?

groups.name: Cellulose
groups.note: Microcrystalline and powdered cellulose, the grades of one material. The cellulose ethers and esters are their own groups.

groups.name: Hypromellose
groups.note: Every viscosity grade of hypromellose (hydroxypropyl methylcellulose), a cellulose ether. Its phthalate and acetate succinate esters are kept apart.

groups.name: Polyethylene glycol
groups.note: Every chain length the labels name (300 to 8000, and the grade not given). The polyethylene glycol esters and ethers are their own groups.

groups.name: Lactose
groups.note: Lactose monohydrate, anhydrous lactose and lactose with no form given.

groups.name: Starch
groups.note: Corn, potato and rice starch. Sodium starch glycolate, maltodextrin and dextrates are made from starch and are their own groups.

groups.name: Iron oxides
groups.note: Red, yellow, black and brown iron oxide are different oxides of iron. The FDA lists them as one colour additive, synthetic iron oxide, which is any one or any combination of them (21 CFR 73.1200), so they are one group here and each is shown.

groups.name: Povidone
groups.note: Every K grade of povidone. Crospovidone (cross-linked) and copovidone (a copolymer) are their own groups.

groups.name: Croscarmellose sodium
groups.note: Cross-linked carboxymethylcellulose sodium, so its own group.

groups.name: Gelatin
groups.note: The labels give one code for gelatin, the FDA's record for gelatin with no type given.

groups.name: Citric acid
groups.note: Anhydrous citric acid and citric acid monohydrate. Its salts are their own groups.

groups.name: Polysorbate 80
groups.note: The other polysorbates (20, 40, 60, 81) are made with other fatty acids and are their own groups.

groups.name: Hydroxypropyl cellulose
groups.note: Every molecular weight grade of hydroxypropyl cellulose, a cellulose ether. Low-substituted hydroxypropyl cellulose is kept apart.

groups.name: Sodium starch glycolate
groups.note: Types A and B, from potato or corn starch. Made from starch by changing it chemically, so its own group.

kept_apart.reason: The registry links hydrated silica to silicon dioxide as its hydrate, which would put it in the group by the rule. It is a different material in use (a precipitated silica), so it is kept apart and shown.
The same polymer as polyethylene glycol at a far greater chain length, sold and named as a different material. Kept apart and shown.
Hydroxypropyl cellulose with far fewer hydroxypropyl groups, a separate pharmacopoeia material that does not dissolve in water. Kept apart and shown.
Low-substituted hydroxypropyl cellulose, kept apart for the same reason.
Mostly sucrose, but a less refined material with other parts of the cane left in. Kept apart and shown.
Sorbitol dissolved in water, a mixture rather than a form of sorbitol. Kept apart and shown.
An ester made from hypromellose: chemically changed, so its own group.
An ester made from hypromellose: chemically changed, so its own group.
An ester made from hypromellose: chemically changed, so its own group.
An ester made from cellulose: chemically changed, so its own group.

A copolymer of povidone's building block with another, so its own group.

selection.chosen_by: A person picked them, brand by brand, in a list kept by hand (products.yaml). Candidates were drafted from the brand names the FDA's Drugs@FDA records give for medicines MoleculeFinder describes, and from brand names added by name (over-the-counter ones too), each with the brand owner's own label, not a repackager's.
selection.gate: A label needs at least three molecules MoleculeFinder holds, matched by the FDA's ingredient code, to have a page on the site.
selection.not_by: They were not chosen by sales, by how often they are prescribed or at random.
